clue.text: Fool keeps boy's horse

indicators.note: a thing that keeps something holds it within, so the fool's word wraps round the boy's

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a fool
Stan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A foolish person hangs on to a lad's horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a wild or half-wild horse of the American plains, so it is one kind of horse.

clue.text: Ms West put stuff in craft

indicators.note: in places the word for stuff inside the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West was a Hollywood actress
to cram is to stuff

explanation.surface: The actress Mae West filled up a handicraft project.
explanation.definitionFit: Macramé is a craft of knotting cord into decorative patterns.

clue.text: Country spy train at odds

indicators.note: odds asks for the odd-numbered letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A nation's agent and its rail network are in conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at odds' looks like a single phrase, but 'at' is part of the letters picked from.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a Middle Eastern nation with Damascus as its capital.

clue.text: Girl taking staple food is deadly sin

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
rice is a staple food for much of the world

explanation.surface: A girl eating basic grub commits one of the cardinal vices.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed, also called avarice, is one of the seven sins of Christian tradition.

clue.text: Told to fix me in dark

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the words are taken by how they are said

parts.note: to glue me is to fix me in place

explanation.surface: Someone is ordered to fasten themselves in the darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy describes poorly lit, shadowy surroundings, so it means dark.

clue.text: Move slowly and don't start to scribble

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter of the word for scribble is dropped

parts.note: to scrawl is to scribble untidily

explanation.surface: Advice to take things gradually and not begin doodling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't start to' removes the S from SCRAWL.
explanation.definitionFit: To crawl is to proceed at a very slow pace, as traffic does in a jam.

clue.text: Ignite fisherman's yield

definitions.meaning: to start burning, as a fire does when it takes hold
the haul of fish brought in by an angler

explanation.surface: A fisherman's haul sets alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire is said to catch when it starts, and an angler's haul is his catch.

clue.text: Fruit from a vine initially, turning firm at a party

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of vine
turning means the abbreviation for firm is read backwards

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Fruit picked off a vine at the start, firming up in time for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is botanically a fruit, a large berry with a single stone.

clue.text: For example, tell tale about vassal

parts.note: to tell a tale is to lie

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the abbreviation for for example is read backwards

explanation.surface: A servant gives an example of tale-telling.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal law a liege could be either the lord or his subject owing allegiance.

clue.text: Get about in ancient Rome?

parts.note: the question asks for the word the Romans used for about, the Latin preposition meaning around or approximately

explanation.surface: A question about travelling around the ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get about' looks like moving around; it really asks for the Latin word that gives 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa is Latin for around or approximately, still used before dates.

clue.text: Result not in, has to arrive

parts.note: someone not in is out
to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: The verdict is not yet in, but has to turn up soon.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or end product of an event, a synonym for result.

clue.text: Reversion to type for a time with poor Mavis

indicators.note: poor suggests the name Mavis is in bad shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Mavis keeps relapsing into old habits for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Atavism is the reappearance of ancestral traits, a throwback to an earlier biological type.

clue.text: Lift man with prayer

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
an Ave, short for Ave Maria, is a Hail Mary prayer

explanation.surface: A man lifts with the help of a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to raise or haul something heavy with effort.

clue.text: Was covetous to contend in the end

indicators.note: in places the word for contend within the word for the end

parts.note: the end is simply END
to vie is to contend or compete

explanation.surface: Someone ended up resentful at having to compete.
explanation.definitionFit: To be covetous is to want what another has, which is to have envied them.

clue.text: Rogue is bad and conceited about it

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for conceited surrounds the word for being bad

parts.note: vain means conceited
someone who is bad, in the sense of poorly, is ill

explanation.surface: A scoundrel is wicked and full of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest scoundrel, the kind of wrongdoer a melodrama casts as its baddie.

clue.text: Make improvements concerning class

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Changes for the better involving a school year group.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform is to amend or correct faults, so it means to improve things.

clue.text: Posh area is redesigned covering two continents

indicators.note: redesigned means given a new layout, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A smart district is remodelled across a huge territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is the combined landmass of Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Sail pole supporting animal, life-jacket needed

indicators.note: supporting here means holding up from around, so the pole encloses the animal

parts.note: a mast is the pole carrying a ship's sails
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A ship's pole holds up an animal that needs a buoyancy aid.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable buoyancy vest from the Second World War, named after a busty actress.

clue.text: Assert positively it's a strong business

parts.note: f is forte, loud or strong, in music
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: Someone declares with certainty that a company is robust.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to state something firmly as true.

clue.text: Old college opening place of tissue growth

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic, a former type of British higher-education college

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from place

explanation.surface: A former college opens a site for studying tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's polytechnics became universities in 1992, hence 'Old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyp is a small abnormal growth of tissue, often in the nose or bowel.

clue.text: Assume, for the sake of argument, one penetrates military base

definitions.text: Assume, for the sake of argument

indicators.note: something that penetrates gets inside, so the numeral goes into the base

parts.note: a post is a military station
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Hypothetically, someone breaks into an army camp.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward a premise as a basis for reasoning.

clue.text: Sound coming from smooth bottle

indicators.note: this asks for a word pronounced like the word that follows

parts.note: to file is to smooth, as with a nail file

explanation.surface: A noise comes from a sleek glass container.
explanation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass vial for medicine or perfume.

clue.text: Predict number and letter on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than seen, so the words are taken by how they are spoken

parts.note: the number four followed by the letter C

explanation.surface: A broadcast gives out a figure and a letter to forecast with.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to anticipate what will happen, so it means to forecast.

clue.text: Work hard and invest pounds inside

indicators.note: inside puts the pound symbol within the word for investing

parts.note: to save is to put money aside, a kind of investing
L, from libra, is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Put in long hours and pour money into the business.
explanation.definitionFit: To slave is to toil long and hard, like someone forced to labour.

clue.text: His wail disturbed language

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters of his and wail are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's troubled cry is in some tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is a Bantu tongue widely spoken in East Africa.

clue.text: First, a geek about to put on for the public

indicators.note: about here means within or around, so the answer sits inside the words before it

explanation.surface: An instruction about which nerd performs first.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage a play is to present or mount it as a performance for an audience.

clue.text: Having a key in Washington a life-saver

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone in the US capital carries a key and a rescue ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonal music is written in a definite key, as opposed to atonal music.

clue.text: Some presume an estimate is the most miserly

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Assuming a rough figure marks out the stingiest person.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft defined 'is the most miserly', but the answer is an adjective; 'is' is a link word, so the definition is 'the most miserly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in British use describes stinginess, so the superlative names the stingiest.
